quote: In the late 1950s, Kuti left [[Lagos]] to study abroad at the London School of Music
Kuti returned to Lagos and played a highlife-jazz hybrid, albeit, without commercial success.
In 1969, Kuti and his band went on a trip to the U.S. and met a woman by the name of Sandra Smith, a singer and former [[Black Panther Party|Black Panther]]
introduced Kuti to many writings of activists such as [[Martin Luther King Jr.]], [[Angela Davis]], [[Jesse Jackson]], and his biggest influence of all, [[Malcolm X]]
That was when Kuti realized that he was not playing African music.
who, with drummer [[Tony Allen (musician)|Tony Allen]], experimented with different contemporary music of that time
Afrobeat was influenced by a combination of different genres, such as [[highlife]], [[Fuji music|fuji]], and [[Jùjú music|jùjú]]
The name was partially born out of an attempt to distinguish Fela Kuti's music from the [[soul music]] of American artists such as [[James Brown]].
Kuti had also changed the name of his group to "[[Africa '70 (band)|Africa '70]]"
The band maintained a five-year residency at the Afrika Shrine from 1970 to 1975
Both worked on [[Talking Heads]]' highly acclaimed 1980 album ''[[Remain in Light]]'', which brought polyrhythmic Afrobeat influences to Western music.
In the late 1990s and early 2000s, a small Afrobeat scene began in [[Brooklyn]], New York, with projects including [[Antibalas]]
